questions.question: Which ship carried the Pilgrims across the Atlantic to New England?
questions.fun_fact: The crossing from Plymouth, England, took about two months, and the ship had earlier carried wine across the Channel.

questions.question: Why did the Pilgrims leave England?
questions.fun_fact: They were Separatists who rejected the Church of England; they lived in the Netherlands for years before sailing.

questions.question: In which present-day US state did the Pilgrims found Plymouth Colony?
questions.fun_fact: They had aimed for the mouth of the Hudson but were blown north and settled at Plymouth in December.

questions.question: What was the Mayflower Compact?

answers.text: A written agreement to govern themselves
A peace treaty with the Wampanoag
The ship's list of cargo and supplies

questions.fun_fact: Forty-one men signed it aboard the ship; it is often called an early step towards self-government in America.

questions.question: Which rock is traditionally said to mark the Pilgrims' landing place?
questions.fun_fact: The link between the boulder and the landing was first made in 1741, over a century after the event.

questions.question: Roughly what share of the Mayflower's passengers died during the first winter at Plymouth?
questions.fun_fact: Disease, cold and hunger took a heavy toll before the first harvest in the new colony.

questions.question: Which Wampanoag leader made a peace agreement with the Plymouth colonists?
questions.fun_fact: The pact reached in spring is remembered as the basis for the Plymouth colonists' first years of survival.

questions.question: Which English-speaking Patuxet man taught the Pilgrims how to plant corn and fish for alewives?
questions.fun_fact: His real name was Tisquantum; he had been abducted to Europe years earlier and learned English there.

questions.question: What does the name 'Wampanoag' mean?
questions.fun_fact: The Wampanoag homeland lies in what is now eastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island, and the people live there to this day.

questions.question: How long did the Plymouth harvest celebration reportedly last?
questions.fun_fact: Edward Winslow wrote that the colonists and their guests feasted and played games for three days.

questions.question: Which Pilgrim wrote the best-known eyewitness account of the Plymouth harvest feast?
questions.fun_fact: His letter was printed in London in a pamphlet known as 'Mourt's Relation'.

questions.question: According to that account, what did the Wampanoag guests bring to the feast?
questions.fun_fact: Venison, wildfowl and corn make up the few foods the written sources actually name.

questions.question: About how many Wampanoag men does Winslow say joined the feast?
questions.fun_fact: The guests outnumbered the surviving colonists, who were only a few dozen, by quite a margin.

questions.question: Which US president declared a national day of thanksgiving in 1789?
questions.fun_fact: Washington set aside a day for gratitude, but it was a one-off and not yet a yearly holiday.

questions.question: Which Founding Father and president declined to issue Thanksgiving proclamations, citing the separation of church and state?
questions.fun_fact: Jefferson argued that the government had no business prescribing religious observances.

questions.question: Which magazine editor campaigned for decades to make Thanksgiving a national holiday?
questions.fun_fact: Hale sent letters to presidents year after year until Lincoln finally acted.

questions.question: Hale edited a famous ladies' magazine. What was it called?
questions.fun_fact: It was one of the most widely read magazines in America in the mid-nineteenth century.

questions.question: Which nursery rhyme is Sarah Josepha Hale traditionally credited with writing?
questions.fun_fact: Who wrote the rhyme has been debated, but Hale is the author most often named.

questions.question: During which war did Abraham Lincoln proclaim a national Thanksgiving?
questions.fun_fact: He asked Americans to give thanks even though the nation was torn apart by battle.

questions.question: Who drafted Lincoln's Thanksgiving proclamation?
questions.fun_fact: Seward wrote the text, and Lincoln signed it in October for a day of thanks in late November.

questions.question: Since 1941, federal law places Thanksgiving on which day?
questions.fun_fact: Congress settled the date after a messy few years in which states disagreed about when to celebrate.

questions.question: Where did the Pilgrims live for years before sailing to America?
questions.fun_fact: They moved to the Dutch city in the 1600s but worried their children were becoming Dutch.

questions.question: Since 1970, many Native Americans gather at Plymouth on Thanksgiving Day for which observance?
questions.fun_fact: The yearly gathering reminds visitors that the holiday has a very different meaning for Native peoples.

questions.question: The Wampanoag leader known to the English as 'King Philip' went by which name?
questions.fun_fact: He was a son of Massasoit and led a war against the colonists in 1675.

questions.question: On which day of the week is Thanksgiving always celebrated in the United States?
questions.fun_fact: The Friday after it is the start of the Christmas shopping season for many.

questions.question: Which bird did Benjamin Franklin reportedly think would have made a better national symbol than the bald eagle?
questions.fun_fact: In a letter to his daughter he called the turkey a more respectable bird, 'a true original native of America'.

questions.question: Which US state raises the most turkeys?
questions.fun_fact: North Carolina usually ranks second.

questions.question: In which region were turkeys first domesticated?
questions.fun_fact: The Aztecs and earlier peoples kept them long before the Spanish carried them across the ocean.

questions.question: What is a male turkey called?
questions.fun_fact: A female is called a hen and the young are called poults.

questions.question: Which red flap of skin hangs from a turkey's throat?
questions.fun_fact: The skin on a male's head and neck changes colour with his mood.

questions.question: Which amino acid in turkey is often blamed for the sleepiness after Thanksgiving dinner?
questions.fun_fact: Chicken has about as much of it; the big meal and the carbohydrates probably matter more.

questions.question: What is a turducken?

answers.text: A turkey stuffed with a duck stuffed with a chicken
A pie made of three kinds of poultry

questions.fun_fact: Football commentator John Madden helped make the dish famous on holiday broadcasts.

questions.question: What is the Butterball Turkey Talk-Line?
questions.fun_fact: It has been answering anxious cooks since 1981, with most calls coming in around late November.

questions.question: What is a 'Tofurky'?

answers.text: A vegetarian holiday roast made from tofu
A turkey baked with tofu stuffing

questions.fun_fact: It was launched in the mid-1990s and has become the best-known meat-free holiday roast.

questions.question: What do many Southerners call stuffing that is baked in a dish instead of in the bird?
questions.fun_fact: Cornbread is a classic base in the South.

questions.question: Which company created the green bean casserole in 1955?
questions.fun_fact: Dorcas Reilly of Campbell's test kitchen came up with the recipe, which calls for cream of mushroom soup and crispy onions.

questions.question: Which topping crowns many American candied sweet potato casseroles?
questions.fun_fact: The sweet dish is more dessert than side, which is why some families fight over it.

questions.question: Cornbread dressing is a traditional part of the Thanksgiving table in which region?
questions.fun_fact: Cornmeal has been a staple of Southern cooking for centuries.

questions.question: Which colonial New England dessert is made from cornmeal, milk and molasses?
questions.fun_fact: It was a way for early colonists to turn cheap cornmeal into something sweet.

questions.question: Which Boston hotel gave its name to a soft, folded dinner roll?
questions.fun_fact: The Omni Parker House, open since 1855, says its kitchen invented the roll.

questions.question: How are many cranberries harvested?

answers.text: The bog is flooded so the berries float
Pickers climb ladders into tall bushes

questions.fun_fact: Cranberries grow on low vines, and air pockets inside the berries make them float.

questions.question: Which US state grows the most cranberries?
questions.fun_fact: Wisconsin has led the country for years, and Massachusetts, where the Pilgrims settled, is also a major producer.

questions.question: Which US state is the biggest producer of pumpkins for canning?
questions.fun_fact: A town in Illinois, Morton, calls itself the 'Pumpkin Capital of the World'.

questions.question: Most 'yams' sold in American supermarkets are really which vegetable?
questions.fun_fact: True yams come from Africa and Asia and are much starchier and drier.

questions.question: What should you do before lowering a turkey into a deep fryer full of hot oil?

answers.text: Make sure it is completely thawed and dry
Keep it frozen so it cooks evenly
Brush it with water so it browns

questions.fun_fact: Water or ice and hot oil is a famously dangerous mix, and fires on Thanksgiving are a common story.

questions.question: Which live attraction featured in the first Macy's parade in New York?

answers.text: Animals from the Central Park Zoo
A troupe of circus acrobats on horseback

questions.fun_fact: Elephants, camels and bears walked the streets before the first balloons arrived a few years later.

questions.question: Which cartoon character was the first giant helium balloon at the Macy's parade?
questions.fun_fact: It floated over the streets in 1927, replacing the animals on loan from the zoo.

questions.question: What was the Macy's parade first billed as?
questions.fun_fact: Its final float was Santa Claus, which is still the closing act today.

questions.question: What happened to the giant balloons at the end of the parade in its early years?

answers.text: They were released into the sky

questions.fun_fact: Finders were offered a prize for returning them, and the practice ended in the early 1930s.

questions.question: Where does the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade end?

answers.text: Macy's flagship store at Herald Square

questions.fun_fact: It starts on the Upper West Side and travels south through Manhattan.

questions.question: Why was the Macy's parade suspended from 1942 to 1944?

answers.text: World War II needed rubber and helium
A polio outbreak hit the city
The store was closed for renovation

questions.fun_fact: Macy's donated the balloons' rubber to the war effort.

questions.question: A runaway balloon of which character injured a spectator in 1997 and led to stricter wind rules?
questions.fun_fact: The balloon struck a lamppost, and rules about wind speeds followed.

questions.question: Which NFL team has played a Thanksgiving game nearly every year since 1934?
questions.fun_fact: The team's owner had the idea so that his struggling club would draw a crowd, and it worked.

questions.question: Which NFL team joined the Thanksgiving tradition in 1966 and became its second regular host?
questions.fun_fact: The Cowboys' general manager wanted a spotlight for the young franchise, and the idea stuck.

questions.question: Which team did the Detroit Lions play in the very first Thanksgiving game in 1934?
questions.fun_fact: The game was broadcast on national radio, and the Bears won a close one.

questions.question: Which undefeated team did the Lions beat on Thanksgiving 1962 after sacking quarterback Bart Starr 11 times?
questions.fun_fact: It was the only loss for the Packers that regular season, and the game is still remembered in Detroit.

questions.question: Which broadcaster began awarding a turkey leg to the best player of the Thanksgiving game?
questions.fun_fact: Madden's turkey leg went to the game's most valuable player, and it later became a trophy named for him.

questions.question: Which show do many Americans watch after the Macy's parade on Thanksgiving morning?

answers.text: The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show

questions.fun_fact: NBC has aired the National Dog Show after the parade since 2002.

questions.question: Which US president carried out the first formal turkey pardon in 1989?
questions.fun_fact: Reagan joked about pardoning a turkey in 1987, and Truman is often credited, though his library denies it.

questions.question: Why did Franklin D. Roosevelt move Thanksgiving a week earlier in 1939?

answers.text: To lengthen the Christmas shopping season

questions.fun_fact: Retailers had lobbied for it, since the holiday would otherwise fall on the last possible date that year.

questions.question: What was Roosevelt's earlier Thanksgiving of 1939 nicknamed?
questions.fun_fact: The country split roughly in half, and some states ended up celebrating twice.

questions.question: What is the origin of the term 'Black Friday'?

answers.text: A blizzard that closed the shops

questions.fun_fact: The term was used in Philadelphia in the 1960s before retailers turned it into a positive.

questions.question: Which company launched Small Business Saturday in 2010?
questions.fun_fact: It comes the day after Black Friday and encourages shopping at local stores.

questions.question: What is GivingTuesday?

answers.text: A charity day following Cyber Monday
A day when shops cut prices on gift cards

questions.fun_fact: It was started in 2012 as a counterweight to the shopping days that precede it.

questions.question: What is 'Friendsgiving'?

answers.text: A Thanksgiving-style meal shared with friends
A charity run on Thanksgiving morning

questions.fun_fact: Everyone usually brings a dish, which turns the dinner into a potluck.

questions.question: What do two people do with a turkey's wishbone?

answers.text: Each pulls an end, and the larger piece gets the wish
They toss it over a shoulder
They hang it on the front door for luck

questions.fun_fact: The custom is much older than Thanksgiving and goes back to ancient Rome and the Etruscans.

questions.question: The Turkey Trot in which city is a YMCA race that claims to be the oldest continuous road race in North America?
questions.fun_fact: It has been run on Thanksgiving Day since 1896, when only a handful of people took part.

questions.question: In the sitcom Friends, which trophy do Ross and Monica fight for in their Thanksgiving football game?
questions.fun_fact: Their competitive streak runs through the show.

questions.question: Which 1987 comedy follows Steve Martin and John Candy as they try to get home for Thanksgiving?
questions.fun_fact: John Hughes wrote and directed it, and the shower-curtain-ring scene is a classic.

questions.question: In 'A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving' (1973), who invites herself and her friends to Charlie Brown's house for dinner?
questions.fun_fact: She does so even though Charlie Brown had planned to spend the day at his grandmother's.

questions.question: What does the Peanuts gang eat for their Thanksgiving dinner in the 1973 special?

answers.text: Toast, popcorn, pretzel sticks and jelly beans
A full turkey with cranberry sauce

questions.fun_fact: Snoopy and Woodstock put the meal together.

questions.question: Which jazz pianist composed the music for the Peanuts TV specials?
questions.fun_fact: His 'Linus and Lucy' is one of the best-known pieces of Peanuts music.

questions.question: Which actress directed the 1995 Thanksgiving comedy-drama 'Home for the Holidays'?
questions.fun_fact: Holly Hunter and Robert Downey Jr. star in the film.

questions.question: In which 1993 comedy does Wednesday Addams wreck a camp's Thanksgiving pageant?
questions.fun_fact: The scene turns the story of the first Thanksgiving upside down.

questions.question: In the animated film 'Free Birds' (2013), what do two turkeys travel back in time to prevent?

answers.text: Turkey being served at the first Thanksgiving
A hunter from shooting the bird

questions.fun_fact: Owen Wilson and Woody Harrelson voice the pair.

questions.question: Which 1947 Christmas classic begins at the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade?
questions.fun_fact: The film used real footage of the parade, with Macy's cooperation.

questions.question: Which Arlo Guthrie song is played on many American radio stations every Thanksgiving?
questions.fun_fact: The story of the song begins with a Thanksgiving dinner and a garbage dump.

questions.question: Which American writer penned the Thanksgiving poem that begins 'Over the river and through the wood'?
questions.fun_fact: It was first printed in 1844 as 'A Boy's Thanksgiving Day'.

questions.question: Which comedian sang 'The Thanksgiving Song' on Saturday Night Live in 1992?
questions.fun_fact: The song lists things to be thankful for, in a deadpan comic way.

questions.question: In the sitcom 'WKRP in Cincinnati', what happens in the famous 'Turkeys Away' episode?

answers.text: The station drops live turkeys from a helicopter
The staff throws a dinner party on the air
A turkey is elected station mascot

questions.fun_fact: The line 'As God is my witness, I thought turkeys could fly' is a classic punchline.

questions.question: Which sitcom gave us the Thanksgiving tradition of 'Slapsgiving'?
questions.fun_fact: It comes from a bet in which Marshall earns the right to slap Barney.

questions.question: Which horror director expanded his 2007 Grindhouse fake trailer into the 2023 feature 'Thanksgiving'?
questions.fun_fact: The trailer was one of several fake trailers shown between the two Grindhouse films.

questions.question: In Canada, on which day is Thanksgiving celebrated?
questions.fun_fact: The Canadian harvest ends earlier than the American one, so the holiday is earlier too.

questions.question: Which English explorer held a thanksgiving service in 1578 that Canadians count as an early North American thanksgiving?
questions.fun_fact: He celebrated after surviving a stormy voyage to the Arctic.

questions.question: Samuel de Champlain founded a winter feasting club in Acadia in 1606. What was it called?

answers.text: The Feast of the Northern Star

questions.fun_fact: Members took turns hunting and cooking for the group to keep spirits up.

questions.question: Which West African country celebrates Thanksgiving on the first Thursday of November?
questions.fun_fact: Its founders were freed African Americans who took the holiday with them.

questions.question: Which Australian territory in the Pacific celebrates Thanksgiving on the last Wednesday of November?
questions.fun_fact: The custom was brought by American whalers in the 19th century.

questions.question: What does Grenada's Thanksgiving Day, on 25 October, commemorate?

answers.text: The founding of its first church

questions.fun_fact: It is a public holiday on the Caribbean island.

questions.question: In which Dutch city is a Thanksgiving service held every year at the Pieterskerk, where Pilgrim pastor John Robinson is buried?
questions.fun_fact: The Pilgrims' time in the city is remembered with a museum and the annual service.

questions.question: Which country observes 'Labor Thanksgiving Day' on 23 November?
questions.fun_fact: It is rooted in an ancient harvest festival and has been a public holiday since 1948.

questions.question: What is the German harvest-thanks festival called?
questions.fun_fact: It is usually celebrated on a Sunday in early October, with churches decorated with crops.

questions.question: Which Korean harvest festival is often called 'Korean Thanksgiving'?
questions.fun_fact: Families gather to share songpyeon rice cakes and honour their ancestors.

questions.question: What red, tart fruit is cooked into the classic sauce served with turkey?
questions.fun_fact: Cranberries were a native food long before the colonists arrived, and are one of few major fruits grown in North America.

questions.question: Which pie is the most iconic Thanksgiving dessert?
questions.fun_fact: The filling is a spiced custard, usually made with canned pumpkin puree.

questions.question: Who traditionally rides the final float of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade?
questions.fun_fact: His arrival marks the unofficial start of the Christmas season in New York.

questions.question: In which year did the Pilgrims and the Wampanoag hold the first Plymouth harvest feast?
questions.fun_fact: Edward Winslow's letter from December of that year is the main source for the feast.

questions.question: How many passengers sailed on the Mayflower in 1620?
questions.fun_fact: A crew of around thirty sailors came along, and about half of the passengers died in the first winter.

questions.question: Roughly how many turkeys do Americans eat on Thanksgiving Day, in millions?
questions.fun_fact: The figure is the National Turkey Federation's yearly estimate.

questions.question: At what internal temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, is a turkey considered safe to eat according to the USDA?
questions.fun_fact: That is about 74 degrees Celsius, measured in the thickest part of the thigh.

questions.question: In which year was the first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade held in New York?
questions.fun_fact: Macy's employees organised it, and many of them were immigrants who wanted to celebrate their new home.
